# t.setContext sets a context of any type: the value is held to the context's
# type, as a provider's is. It was declared over two strings, so an int or a
# struct context could not be set from a test at all ("cannot pass int as
# string").

sngl test --platform none setctx.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go setctx.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform html setctx.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- setctx.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

context #depth(1)

struct Theme {
    primary string
}

context #theme(Theme{primary="blue"})

func show() => "{depth}:{theme.primary}"

component main node {
    func probe() => show()
    text(value=probe())
}

func testSetInt(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.probe() == "1:blue")
    t.setContext(depth, 5)
    t.assert(c.probe() == "5:blue")
}

func testSetStruct(t Test, c main) {
    t.setContext(theme, Theme{primary="red"})
    t.assert(c.probe() == "1:red")
}

window {
    main
}
